summary: Dripmetric is a revenue-leak detector for self-serve SaaS. It reads product usage and, optionally, payment events together, watches for nine kinds of revenue leak (such as onboarding stalls, trials that end unpaid and likely buyers who go quiet), scores how close each user is to buying, and sends alerts to Slack or Discord plus a weekly leak report. It needs no billing integration. It is in private beta, free during the beta, with a waitlist.
inventory_evidence: Next.js app in apps/site: the routes / (src/app/page.tsx), /about, /privacy, /leaks, /buying-intent, /docs, /guides, /guides/trial-to-paid-conversion, /compare and /compare/posthog (src/app/**/page.tsx) are the only canonical pages; every page except / and /privacy renders content/pages/*.md. /pricing, /login, /signup and /dashboard are permanent redirects to the home page, not pages; unknown paths, /terms included, render src/app/not-found.tsx with a 404 status.
refresh_trigger: Regenerate with `pnpm site:markdown` whenever src/content/site.ts, a section in src/components/home, the privacy page or a file in content/pages changes, and set updated_at on every page whose words changed: sitemap.xml takes its lastmod from it. The other pages are rendered from the same Markdown files, so their copies cannot drift; review content/index.body.md against the rendered home page first.
